basis: Developmental and intellectual disability define syndrome; hypermetropia 38% and strabismus 30% support ocular involvement. Joint hypermobility alone does not establish tissue damage.
Umbrella skeletal dysplasia; endocrine and cardiac disease are subtype-specific.
Syndromic developmental and intellectual disability; structural cardiac abnormalities occur in roughly 30-50%. Skeletal abnormalities vary across the umbrella.
Congenital skeletal muscle disease with weakness and hypotonia. Infantile apnea reflects neuromuscular dysfunction and does not establish intrinsic airway or lung damage.
B-lineage acute leukemia involving blood and marrow; lymphoid lineage alone does not establish a separate lymphoma or immune mechanism.
Isolated familial dilated cardiomyopathy; myocardial dysfunction defines the disease.
Congenital myopathy and joint contractures define disease. Frequent respiratory insufficiency reflects respiratory muscle weakness and restrictive skeletal mechanics.
Inflammatory disease of retinal blood vessels defines ocular involvement, vascular involvement and an immune or infectious mechanism.
Pathological choroidal vessels invade ocular tissue and impair vision; no extraocular vascular involvement is established.
Developmental disability and ocular anomalies define syndrome; nystagmus 60%, ptosis 40%. Sensorineural hearing impairment affects 2/4 patients.
Clonal marrow proliferation defines PV. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction; thromboses and hypertension are separate diagnoses.
Congenital hypoplastic anemia and intellectual disability define syndrome; unspecified congenital anomalies do not support additional axes.
Dystonia-parkinsonism is a central movement disorder; common dysphagia and drooling reflect bulbar neurological dysfunction.
Congenital cleft of the oral commissure produces an abnormally wide mouth; the mouth belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Intellectual disability, psychomotor delay and polydactyly are principal features. Hemangioma frequency is unspecified; cardiac and urogenital defects are only reported.
Severe inherited peripheral neuropathy; denervation muscle wasting and persistent foot deformities affect most patients. Ocular findings are occasional.
Selective antibody deficiency defines immune dysfunction; associated infections are separate diseases and organ damage is not universal across isotypes.
APRIL deficiency causes antibody immunodeficiency; no common direct extraimmune organ damage is established by the supplied phenotype.
Congenital fusion and duplication of digits directly affect the skeletal system.
Mixed-lineage acute leukemia is a blood and marrow neoplasm; BCR-ABL1 does not independently establish another organ axis.
Poorly specified inherited plasma proteolysis phenotype; assignment to the blood axis is provisional because no clinical definition or phenotype is supplied.
Superficial sweat duct obstruction produces vesicles within the stratum corneum; disease is confined to skin.
Umbrella category of acute myeloid blood and marrow neoplasms; extrahematologic infiltration is not common across the group.
Congenital dysgenesis of the corpus callosum directly affects brain structure.
Alphavirus infection defines the umbrella. Persistent arthritis and encephalitis vary by viral subtype and are not established across most patients.
